div.l: The rule of seint Maure and of seint Benet
Be cause it was olde and som dele streite
This Monke lete olde þinges passe
And held aftre þe newe world þe space
He gaf not of the texte a pulled henne
That seith that hunters beth no holi men̄
Nor that a Monke whan he is rechelese
Is likened to a fissh whan he is waterlese
This is to sey a monk whan he is oute of his cloistr
But þat text held he not worth and oystr
And I seid his opinion was goode
What shuld he studi and make him self wode
Vpon̄ aboke alwey in cloistr to pour
Or swynke with his hondez and laboure
As Austin did . but how shal þe world be ʆserued
Late him haue his swinke to him reserued
Therefor he was a prikasoure a right
Grehoundez he hadde as swift as foule in flight
Of priking and of hunting of þe hare
Was al his lust for no þing wold he spare
I sagh his sleues purfeled atte hande
And for to festen̄ his hode vnder his chyn̄
He had of gold wrought a curious pyn̄
A loue knot on þe grettest ende was
His hede was balled that shone as glas
And eke his face as he hadde be a noynte
He was a lord full fat and in gode poynte
His eyen stepe and rolling in his hede
That semed as a furneis of lede
His botez soupell his horse in grete state
Now certeinly he was a fair prelate
He was not pale as a forpeined gooste
A fat swan loued he best of any roste
His palferay was as brown̄ as is a bery
A Frere ther was a wantoıı̄un and a mery
A lymetour and a ful solempn̄e man̄
In al þe orders iiij . is none þat can
So moche of Dalience and fair langage
He had made many a faire mariage
Of yonge wymmen̄ at his own̄ coste
Vnto his ordre he was a noble poste
Ful wel loued and ful famulier was he
With þe Frankeleyns ouer al in his contre
